# The Tale of the First Shadow

Long ago, when the world was newly formed, there lived a curious child named Lumina who glowed with inner light. In those ancient days, all beings shone brilliantly, and darkness did not exist.

One day, Lumina discovered a mysterious stone that absorbed light rather than reflected it. Fascinated, she held it close to her chest. For the first time, a dark silhouette appeared on the ground behind her—the world's first shadow.

The other luminous beings gasped in horror. "You have brought darkness into our perfect world!" they cried, banishing Lumina to the edge of existence.

Alone and dimmed, Lumina wept. Her tears fell upon the shadow, and something miraculous happened. The shadow began to dance, swirling into beautiful shapes—animals, trees, and stories that flickered across the ground.

Lumina realized that shadows were not evil, but contrast. They gave depth to the flat world and made light itself visible. Without darkness, brightness had no meaning.

She returned to her people and showed them shadow puppets, eclipses, and the gentle relief of shade on a hot day. The beings understood, and from that day forward, light and shadow existed in harmony.

And Lumina? She became the first storyteller, forever playing with light and dark.

This saddened Aurelia deeply, for she longed to create something lasting that would bring joy to the world below. One winter evening, she wept tears of pure starlight that froze as they fell through the frigid northern air.

The Sky Father, moved by her sorrow, granted her a gift. He transformed her frozen tears into ribbons of dancing light—emerald greens, violet purples, and shimmering blues. These became her new threads.

Now, Aurelia weaves her tapestries across the northern skies, and unlike her previous work, these creations remain visible for all to see. The people below named them the Northern Lights, never knowing they watch an eternal artist painting her masterpiece across the heavens, night after magical night.
